problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination
examples.problem:
Consider the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042052/assets/4749f1e50cf7768f39d26737bfce4d9e8e85d5b350f4bc9844a358cd4c3c5cc0.png)

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=7\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042052/assets/a4e5c5eba6d2d8b30955668d47bb2a131c702cc7ec62ef7dada9ed9ad60d8182.png)

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=6\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the first and the second equation we get

$$
-2{x}_{2}=-8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=4.
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & =-7 \\ {x}_{1}-(4) & =-7 \\ {x}_{1} & =-7+4 \\ {x}_{1} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =6 \\ 2(-3)+3(4) & =6 \\ 6 & =6,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ which means

$$
-3{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+4=1.
$$
